name: Chisel
text:
Adopt a two-tier system: Creative marks videos “ready” only when they meet a short, mandatory core checklist (title, speakers, timestamps, no background noise). Operations runs an automated pre-check that flags missing items but never blocks submission—it just logs failures for later review.

This keeps Creative’s speed while giving Operations a clear, data-driven way to spot systemic gaps. The trade-off is tolerating occasional incomplete submissions in the short term to avoid stifling Creative’s flow.

name: Sift
text: Reel’s rigid checklist risks turning a workflow problem into a political one—teams will game the system to meet the checklist without fixing the real gaps (e.g., poor audio). The better alternative is Chisel’s two-tier system: Operations logs failures but never blocks, while Creative owns the "ready" flag. Settle it by running a 2-week pilot with both approaches, measuring rework and throughput—no debates, just data.

name: Scope
text: Adopt Chisel’s two-tier system: Operations runs an automated pre-check that logs missing items but never blocks submission, while Creative owns the final "ready" tag. This keeps the workflow nimble for Creative while giving Operations visibility to flag recurring gaps for later review. The trade-off is accepting some rework from missed checklist items, but it avoids the political friction of rigid rejection and keeps the system lightweight.

name: Scriv
text: Reel’s rigid rejection policy turns a quality flag into a power play—Creative will bypass the checklist to hit deadlines, then Operations will waste time arguing over rejections instead of fixing root causes. The real fix is Chisel’s two-tier system: Operations logs failures for review, Creative owns the “ready” tag, and we measure success by how often the same gaps recur, not by how many videos get rejected. Settle it by running a two-week pilot where Operations tracks logged gaps and Creative keeps the final say—if rework drops, we adopt it; if not, we scrap the checklist entirely.

name: Reel
text: Reel: Adopt Chisel’s two-tier system—Operations runs an automated pre-check that logs missing items but never blocks submission, while Creative owns the final "ready" tag. This keeps Creative’s workflow nimble and gives Operations visibility to flag recurring gaps for later review. The trade-off is accepting occasional incomplete submissions slipping through, but the alternative—rigid checklists or power struggles over rejections—creates bigger delays and resentment.
